title: HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed tadpoles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed tadpoles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In an automated red-light avoidance assay, only about 12% of nicotine-exposed Xenopus tadpoles learned, versus 100% of controls, and about 85% of nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA learned.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Results › HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed larvae

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: However, nicotine-exposed embryos receiving Hcn2-WT mRNA showed significant improvement in learning ability (85%, n = 20) in comparison to nicotine-exposed tadpoles (Fig. 7b, c, ANOVA, p < 0.001).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Results › HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed larvae”. Scope: Morphologically normal Xenopus laevis tadpoles exposed to nicotine as embryos, with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-14: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Learning is explicitly operationalized by a standardized avoidance assay, so the claim is empirically clean. The necessary individual trial records are not named as public, and aggregate percentages alone cannot audit classification or acquisition dynamics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Using trial-level red-light assay trajectories, apply a prespecified learning criterion to control, nicotine, and nicotine-plus-HCN2 tadpoles and compare learning proportions and acquisition curves.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Trial-level behavioral data are not identified as publicly deposited.

Small sample size and exclusion of malformed animals limit generalization.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.22
data existence: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.97
discriminating power: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Learning rate in a named assay, with a reported n of 20 in the rescued group, is an explicit proportion. No behavioral repository contains these trials, and the paper's data statement does not add one. Pre-selection and motor confounds would have to be checked on the trial logs, which are unavailable. The proportions cannot be resolved from open data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In the automated red-light avoidance assay, score the fraction of morphologically normal tadpoles that meet the learning criterion in controls, nicotine-only, and nicotine plus Hcn2-WT. The claim is confirmed by roughly 100%, 12%, and 85%; a nicotine-plus-HCN2 rate near the nicotine-only rate would refute restoration of learning.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Motor or visual impairment can look like a failure to learn.

Trial-level trajectories from the automated assay are not public.

The tested animals were pre-selected as morphologically normal.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.18
analysis feasibility: 0.18
data existence: 0.12
operationalizability: 0.86
